summary: Geoff Childs is a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist who earned his PhD from Indiana University, studying under Tsetan Chonjore. He held an Andrew Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship at Australian National University and was Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Washington University in St. Louis.

Geoffrey Barstow works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held a post at the University of Virginia from circa 2007 to 2013 and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Oregon State University around 2013.

Geoffrey Goble works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned an MA at the University of Virginia and a PhD from Indiana University, later serving as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Oklahoma.

Geoffrey Samuel, a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Leach, Tambiah, and Wilson. His posts included Lancaster University, the University of Newcastle, and Cardiff University as Emeritus Professor.

Georg Buddruss was an Indologist and linguist who also worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt and the University of Tübingen, later serving as Professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from circa 1964 to 1997.

Georg Bühler (1837–1898) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey and Hermann Sauppe at the University of Göttingen. He held posts at Elphinstone College, Bombay Presidency, and Deccan College before taking a chair at the University of Vienna.

Linguist Georg Curtius studied under Ritschl and Lassen at the University of Bonn and under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Charles University and the University of Kiel before becoming professor of classical philology at Leipzig University.

Georg Morgenstierne was a linguist specializing in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Oslo and under Sten Konow, later holding an academic post at the University of Gothenburg from circa 1930 to 1937.

Georg Wilhelm Freytag was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at the University of Göttingen from circa 1811 to 1815 and the University of Bonn from circa 1819 to 1861.

Georg von Simson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as an editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1968 and was a professor at the University of Oslo from circa 1977 to 2003.

Georg von der Gabelentz was a linguist and sinologist who studied at the University of Jena and Leipzig University. He served as Professor of the languages of Eastern Asia at Leipzig University and later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin.

George A. Keyworth is a specialist in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. Educated at UC Santa Barbara and UCLA (PhD 2001 under Robert E. Buswell Jr.), he held a professorship at the University of Colorado Boulder and later joined the University of Saskatchewan.
George Abraham Grierson was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He was educated at St. Bees School and Trinity College Dublin, and he served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1873 to 1903.

George Baumann is an Indologist who completed his PhD at Heidelberg University. He served as Head of the Oriental Department at Tübingen University Library from 1976 to 2001 and held a post at the University of Tübingen.

George Cardona was an Indologist and linguist who studied at New York University and Yale University. He served as a fellow at the Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences and spent his career as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania.

George Chemparathy was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Paul Hacker and Erich Frauwallner. He held an appointment at Loyola College, Chennai, and served as a professor at Utrecht University from circa 1973 to 1993.

George Cœdès was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1906 to 1911. By 1934, he served as president of the Société des Amis du Vieux Hanoi.

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD at Northwestern University, where he served as Professor of Religion from circa 1974 to 2012.

George Foot Moore was a religious studies scholar who studied at Yale University from circa 1868 to 1872. He served as a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (circa 1883–1902) and at Harvard University (circa 1902–1928).

George L. Hart is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard University from circa 1963 to 1969. He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1969 to 1975 before serving as a professor at UC Berkeley from circa 1975 to 2014.
